VibePascal v58 Linux x86_64 compiler -- a .ppu shorter than its header says is truncated
Source commit: dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a
Parent release: v57 (1f605f41b3b06a5fa84fb4cb31ee4298fb30907f)
Built: 2026-09-11, native self-host fixpoint on x86_64-linux (stage1==stage2==stage3)
ppcx64 md5:    8C8179B2F0A452CEBEC0131AA301B076
ppcx64 sha256: DF34EFC40B4F8717E3F221A9CC175C66BA7D5222DB39FC520BA67EC31A7D0991
ppudump md5:   241AB27A8991E3F599FA7A5564AF30A2   (rebuilt: it shares the same reader)

Contents: bin/ppcx64 and bin/ppudump -- a COMPILER-BINARY refresh meant to drop
into an existing VibePascal source/unit tree on Linux.  No RTL change, no
package change, no PPU format change, so an existing v52..v57 Linux unit set
stays valid and does not need rebuilding.

WHAT WAS BROKEN
---------------
This is the gap v57's own VERSION.txt declared under "NOT FIXED, AND NOT
HIDDEN", now closed.

v57 stopped the compiler HANGING on a half-written .ppu, but it only ever
noticed damage it happened to trip over.  Lose the TAIL of a unit file and there
was nothing to trip over: nothing an interface load reads lives in the last
handful of bytes, so the compiler read what it wanted, never reached the missing
part, and built your program against a unit that is not all there -- exit 0, no
message, nothing to search a log for.  Measured on a real 55291-byte unit, every
truncation from 55271 bytes upward was accepted.

A killed build, a full disk or an interrupted copy is exactly how a file loses
its tail, so this is the same accident v57 was about, landing a few bytes later.

WHAT CHANGED
------------
A .ppu header records how long the payload is, so a complete unit file is always
exactly 40 bytes of header plus that number, and can never be fewer.  Nothing
compared those two numbers; the reader checked only that the file was big enough
to hold the header and then trusted whatever followed.  tppufile.readheader now
compares them and rejects a SHORT file.  Longer than declared stays legal, as it
always was.  The arithmetic is 64-bit on purpose: the declared size is an
unsigned 32-bit field, and a corrupt header claiming near 4 GB would wrap a
32-bit sum and switch the check off at exactly the moment it is needed.

THIS DOES NOT TURN GOOD BUILDS RED.  The rejection is soft and self-healing:
  * if the unit's source is available, the unit is RECOMPILED and the build goes
    green -- measured, the .ppu comes back at its full length;
  * if a good copy of the same unit sits in a later -Fu directory, the compiler
    falls through to it and the build goes green -- also measured;
  * only a truncated unit with no source and no other copy stops the compile, and
    it stops with the message an absent unit already gives.
Nobody is ever told to go and delete a file.

The other half of the change is that the length has to BE a length.  It came
from Seek-to-end, which only a plain file answers with a byte count -- a range
stream (a .ppu read from inside a package file) answers with its last valid
offset, one short.  Left alone, that would have declared every packaged unit
truncated by exactly one byte.  The length is now handed in by whoever opens the
stream and knows it, and the range stream's own seek is left alone rather than
bent to serve a reader that does not need it.  Said plainly: no target in this
compiler enables dynamic packages, so that package half cannot be exercised here
and is written to be right if it is ever switched on, not proven by running it.

VERIFIED
--------
  * 4000 real .ppu files in rtl/ and packages/: every one is exactly 40+declared
    bytes, so the check has no slack to fire falsely on
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh, extended this release to SCORE the tail offsets
    it used to document as an open gap:
        20/25 offsets clean, 5 problem(s), exit 1   on the pre-fix compiler
        25/25 offsets clean, 0 problem(s), exit 0   on this one
  * dist/unit-set-loadcheck.sh x86_64-linux: 147/147 packages load clean
  * full 1983-test corpus A/B against a baseline rebuilt from this same source
    with the same command minus the patch: 1983 SAME, 0 DIFF
  * self-host fixpoint: stage1 == stage2 == stage3, byte-identical

NOTE ON bin/ppudump: it is STRIPPED in this release and was not in v57, which is
why it is about 1.2 MB smaller.  Nothing else about it changed -- its output on
an intact .ppu is byte-identical to v57's, and .text differs by under 0.1%.  On a
truncated .ppu it now refuses the file up front instead of dumping partway and
ending in "!! Error in PPU".
